episodes.script: Did you know? A name alone isn't enough for the Death Note to work. Light must picture the person's face while writing their real name. Without that rule, two strangers with the same name could be in danger. Imagine two people called Alex. The notebook sees the same letters. So which Alex is the target? Here's the twist. The writer must connect that name to one specific face. No face in mind? The notebook doesn't activate. Suddenly, hidden identities become a real defense against Kira. A masked stranger is harder to identify. A fake name creates another obstacle. And a famous face? That could make someone easier to target. The world's scariest notebook has a weakness: it still needs information. Would you hide your face or your name from Kira? Tell me below, and subscribe to Otaku Reframe for more anime secrets!
episodes.editorial_note: Canon rule: writer must picture the intended person's face while writing their name. Shared names alone never affect all people; no explicit violence. Does not retell the published EP01.
episodes.description:
Your name alone can't activate the Death Note. The writer needs your face too. But what happens when two people share the same name? Discover one of Death Note's most important rules, then decide: would you hide your face or your name from Kira? Subscribe to Otaku Reframe for more anime mysteries!

#DeathNote #Anime #Shorts
